candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — safe medication preparation and administration
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — insulin device selection
candidate.educational_objective: Use a U-100 insulin syringe with vial-based U-100 insulin to avoid unit-to-volume dosing errors.

options.A: A U-100 insulin syringe calibrated for U-100 insulin.
options.B: Any 1-mL syringe because insulin units and milliliters are interchangeable.
options.C: A tuberculin syringe without a prescribed unit-to-volume conversion plan.
options.D: Any syringe chosen only by needle length because barrel calibration does not affect dosing.

candidate.rationale: HUMULIN R U-100 contains 100 units/mL. Its Instructions for Use specify a U-100 insulin syringe and warn that use of the wrong syringe can cause dosing errors. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: HUMULIN R U-100 vial administration requires a U-100 insulin syringe; mismatched syringe calibration can cause dosing error.
candidate.source_document_title: HUMULIN R (insulin human) injection, U-100 — Vial Instructions for Use
candidate.source_locator: Humulin R U-100 Vial Instructions for Use — Supplies needed; package carton 'Use only with a U-100 syringe'
candidate.source_version_date: Instructions for Use revised June 2022; current label checked 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: A client is drawing HUMULIN R U-100 insulin from a vial for subcutaneous injection. Which syringe should the nurse instruct the client to use?
